actions.create_label.description: Creates a new label in FeedHive for organising posts.
actions.create_label.props.title.descrip: The name of the label (e.g. "Campaign Q1", "Evergreen Content").
actions.create_post.description: Creates a new post in FeedHive (draft or scheduled).
actions.create_post.props.accounts.descr: Select the social media accounts to publish this post to.
actions.create_post.props.labels.descrip: Optionally assign labels to organise this post in FeedHive.
actions.create_post.props.notes.descript: Private notes visible only to your team in FeedHive. Not published.
actions.create_post.props.scheduled_at.d: Required when Status is "Scheduled". The exact date and time the post should be published.
actions.create_post.props.short_link_ena: Automatically shorten URLs in your post text.
actions.create_post.props.status.descrip: Choose "Draft" to save without scheduling, or "Scheduled" to set a publish date.
actions.create_post.props.text.descripti: The main content of your post.
actions.custom_api_call.description: Make a custom API call to a specific endpoint
actions.custom_api_call.props.failsafe.d: On a failed request, output the error instead of failing the step.
actions.custom_api_call.props.followRedi: Follow 3xx redirects instead of returning them as the response.
actions.custom_api_call.props.headers.de: Authorization headers are injected automatically from your connection.
actions.custom_api_call.props.response_i: Enable for files like PDFs, images, etc.
actions.custom_api_call.props.timeout.de: Seconds to wait for a response. Empty: up to the flow limit (10 min).
actions.delete_post.description: Deletes a post from FeedHive. This action cannot be undone.
actions.delete_post.props.post_id.descri: Select the post you want to act on.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.descriptio: Fires a FeedHive Workflow Trigger to create a post. The workflow defines which accounts to post to, the AI model to use, and any default content.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.link: A URL to attach to the post — only applicable for YouTube, Google My Business, and Pinterest posts.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.medi: Public URLs of images or videos to include in the post (e.g. https://example.com/photo.jpg).
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.prom: Ask FeedHive AI to generate the post content. Only used if your workflow is configured for AI generation.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.sche: When to publish the post. Leave empty to use the schedule defined in the workflow.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.setu:
### How to find your Trigger ID

1. In FeedHive, open the **Workflows** section in the sidebar.
2. Open the workflow you want to fire.
3. In the workflow settings, copy the **Trigger ID** (a short alphanumeric code).

**Note:** You can also pass custom template variables — if your workflow content contains placeholders like `[[first_name]]`, add them in the **Template Variables** field below.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.temp: If your workflow template uses placeholders like [[first_name]], provide them here as key-value pairs (e.g. first_name → John). Each key maps directly to a [[placeholder]] in your template.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.text: The content of the post. Leave empty to let your workflow generate or use a template.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.titl: Post title — only applicable for YouTube, Google My Business, and Pinterest posts.
actions.fire_workflow_trigger.props.trig: The ID of your FeedHive workflow trigger. Found in FeedHive → Workflows → your workflow settings.
actions.get_post.description: Retrieves the details of a specific post.
actions.get_post.props.post_id.descripti: Select the post you want to act on.
actions.list_posts.description: Returns a list of posts, optionally filtered by status or labels.
actions.list_posts.props.labels.descript: Optionally assign labels to organise this post in FeedHive.
actions.list_posts.props.limit.descripti: Maximum number of posts to return. Between 1 and 100.
actions.list_posts.props.status.descript: Only return posts with this status. Leave empty to return all posts.
actions.update_post.description: Updates an existing post in FeedHive. Only the fields you fill in will be changed.
actions.update_post.props.accounts.descr: Select the social media accounts to publish this post to.
actions.update_post.props.labels.descrip: Optionally assign labels to organise this post in FeedHive.
actions.update_post.props.notes.descript: Update the private notes for this post.
actions.update_post.props.post_id.descri: Select the post you want to act on.
actions.update_post.props.scheduled_at.d: Update the scheduled publish date and time.
actions.update_post.props.short_link_ena: Automatically shorten URLs in the post text.
actions.update_post.props.status.descrip: Change the post status. Leave empty to keep the current status.
actions.update_post.props.text.descripti: The new content of the post. Leave empty to keep the current text.
auth.description:
To get your FeedHive API key:
1. Log in to your FeedHive account.
2. Go to **Settings** → **Account** (or **Workspace**).
3. Find the **API Key** section and copy your key.

Your key starts with `fh_`.
description: Schedule, manage and publish social media content with FeedHive.
triggers.comment_notification.descriptio: Triggers when a comment is added to one of your posts.
triggers.comment_notification.props.inst:
### Setup Instructions

1. Enable this flow and copy the **Webhook URL** shown below.
 ```text
  {{webhookUrl}}
  ```
2. In FeedHive, go to **Settings → Automation → Notifications**.
3. Click **Create New Notification**.
4. Choose **Comment Added** and paste the Webhook URL, then click **Save**.
triggers.post_notification.description: Triggers when a post is published, scheduled, or fails.
triggers.post_notification.props.event_t: Choose the event type you will configure in FeedHive. This is used to load sample data when testing the trigger — it does not filter incoming webhooks.
triggers.post_notification.props.instruc:
### Setup Instructions

1. Enable this flow and copy the **Webhook URL** shown below.
 ```text
  {{webhookUrl}}
  ```
2. In FeedHive, go to **Settings → Automation → Notifications**.
3. Click **Create New Notification**.
4. Choose the matching event type and paste the Webhook URL, then click **Save**.
